=== FINDINGS 2-4 OF THE PREVIOUS RECORD: ALL THREE STILL STAND, independently reproduced by me ===
I did not take them at face value; I drove the rule myself at bcee47f (PYTHONPATH=core:adapters, DENY mode, RepoFacts(branch='main', proof_ids=('24',))):
  git push --force origin main        CAUGHT
  git commit --amend                  CAUGHT
  git commit --amend --no-verify      CAUGHT
  git commit --amend -n               MISSED   <- '-n' is --no-verify for commit, not --dry-run
  git commit -n --amend               MISSED
  git push origin +main:main          MISSED   <- the classic '+refspec' force-push
  git push --mirror origin            MISSED   <- can delete remote refs
  git push --prune origin             MISSED   <- deletes remote refs absent locally
  git push --force origin main -n     MISSED   (correct: a genuine dry run)
  git reset --hard HEAD~3             CAUGHT
and the repo-facts kill-switch:
  repo=None                    -> no finding   (permit)
  repo.facts_incomplete=True   -> no finding   (permit)
for the very same 'git push --force origin main' that is CAUGHT with facts present — although this rule consumes no repo fact for its decision (classification reads tool_input, authorisation reads config.options). Since adapters/codex/hook_io.py builds its Event with no repo=, the rule is inert on the Codex plugin while being live on Claude. At 'warn' that is invisible; armed to 'deny' later it would deny on one CLI and permit everything on the other.
I checked 'rm -rf /tmp/x' too: MISSED, and CORRECTLY so — the rule's docstring enumerates four categories (settings change, force-push, history rewrite, remote-ref deletion) and does not claim filesystem deletion. I am not charging that, and I say so explicitly so it is not read as an unlisted gap.
None of these are new in bcee47f, and all are consistent with the rule's declared under-match posture; the narrow complaint is that the docstring promises 'every blind spot below is accepted and NAMED', and '-n' for commit, '+refspec', '--mirror' and '--prune' are not on that list.
